events.content:
The home page is now a server component that shows a welcome message and logs each page view using after() from next/server. That's the approach recommended in the Next.js docs bundled with this project for work that runs after the response is sent. npx next build finished with exit code 0, and / shows up as a dynamic route. I didn't start the server or check that an analytics event actually gets sent.

- app/page.tsx: an async server component that reads the user-agent and referer headers while the page renders. It then schedules logPageView(...) inside after(), so logging runs once the response is done and doesn't slow the page down. The headers have to be read before after(): the docs say calling headers() or cookies() inside the after callback in a server component throws a runtime error.
- app/lib/analytics.ts: logPageView() sends a page_view event with a POST to the URL in the ANALYTICS_ENDPOINT environment variable. If that variable isn't set, it just writes the event to the console. Errors are caught and logged, so a failed analytics call won't cause problems.

Reading headers is what makes / render on each request. Without that, the docs say the callback would run once at build time instead of on each visit.

The build also changed tsconfig.json on its own: it set jsx to react-jsx and added .next/dev/types//.ts to include.
